reason: DeviceMonitoringService.cs:173 now passes the token, and the only handler that catches OperationCanceledException is catch (Exception) at :184, which returns false. So shutdown mid-cycle logs spurious warnings, and a device that was already offline finishes without the cancellation being propagated. I lowered this from medium: the false-offline write to the database is blocked because AppDbService.cs:35 calls SaveChangesAsync with the already-cancelled token, and ExecuteAsync:58 still exits on the token check.
claim: Cancelling during SendPingAsync lands in the generic catch (Exception). That catch logs a Warning and returns false, so the cancellation becomes an 'offline' result.
evidence: SendPingAsync(..., cancellationToken: cancellationToken) throws OperationCanceledException when the token is cancelled. The only handler that catches it is `catch (Exception ex) { _logger.LogWarning(ex, "Unexpected error pinging {IpAddress}", ipAddress); return false; }`, so the exception is not rethrown. CheckDeviceAsync then sees `device.IsOnline != isOnline`, sets IsOnline=false and OnlineSince=null, and calls UpdatePcDeviceAsync(device, cancellationToken). The save is probably stopped only because SaveChangesAsync throws on the already-cancelled token. Nothing filters this case, e.g. `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) { throw; }`.

reason: Dockerfile:33 installs iputils-ping the same unpinned way as the existing gosu package, and the comment at :31 says why it is needed. Ping is the dependency the change is meant to add, so this is not a defect of the change.
claim: iputils-ping is added to the runtime image without a version pin.
evidence: `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gosu iputils-ping` has no version pin. The app runs as appuser via `exec gosu appuser "$@"` in docker-entrypoint.sh, so .NET's Ping falls back to the external ping utility, and this package supplies it. It is a necessary new runtime dependency and should be recorded as one.
